item.title: Steve Lacy Didn’t Rush SZA & Got Her Verse Before Turning The Song In
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Steve Lacy said he did not want to rush SZA, whose verse arrived as he was about to turn in their collaboration.
item.content:encoded:
Steve Lacy said he did not rush SZA for a verse. It arrived as he was about to turn their song in.

The singer shared the story in an October 21 clip from “The Drew Barrymore Show.”

“I wanted this verse, but I waited. I didn’t want to force it,” he said.

Lacy said they’d known each other for a couple of years. A mutual friend connected them. He described bringing a laptop and instruments to see what she needed.

While SZA wrote to his beats, he offered pointers and reminded her about his own song. He considered writing the part himself rather than pushing her.

The song “Is It Cool?” appears on Lacy’s third album, “Oh Yeah?”. RCA Records released the 10-track project on July 17. Its guests also include Erykah Badu and Cecile Believe.

Lacy said writing can mean waiting for inspiration, with lyrics taking longer to find than sounds on an instrument.

Lacy had described another wait for a collaborator in a 2023 Guitar World interview. The story concerned the making of “Pride,” which he co-wrote and co-produced for Kendrick Lamar’s 2017 album.

Lacy said DJ Dahi had invited him into the sessions, where Dahi played drum loops and he added basslines or guitar riffs. When he got a moment alone with Kendrick, he played a song he had started with Anna Wise. He had taken their acoustic version home and put a beat behind it.

Kendrick liked it, but Lacy said he left the song with him without pressing for an answer. He was in London when a leaked tracklist finally showed his name in the credits. Until then, he had not expected Kendrick to use it.

The same interview laid out what Lacy valued in a session: making people comfortable, reading the room and finding a creative fit. He said being willing to offer an idea, even an unusual one, mattered alongside the ability to play. His goal was to keep the exchange moving while giving everyone room to contribute.

His “Oh Yeah? Tour” is next scheduled to stop in Charlotte, North Carolina, on October 22.

item.title: Damon Dash’s Past Gets A Price Tag As Creditors Come Calling
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Damon Dash's life-story auction drew a $550,000 winning bid, with a $500,000 backup offer if the deal failed to close.
item.content:encoded:
Damon Dash‘s life story drew a $550,000 winning bid at auction, with the money meant for his creditors rather than the Roc-A-Fella co-founder.

Bankruptcy trustee Traci K. Stevenson served notice of the result on October 21. The reported notice named Everlasting Films LLC as the October 1 auction winner.

The package included exclusive worldwide life-story rights, 100 hours of video, photos and memorabilia, plus an unfinished documentary or film project. The plan allowed the buyer to make movies, documentaries or books, not just one production.

Everlasting had opened with a $37,000 offer. Its winning bid came after years of creditors seeking payment through Dash’s assets.

The legal fight with filmmaker Josh Webber began over “Dear Frank.” A New York jury found Dash liable for copyright infringement in 2022. Webber later won a separate $4 million defamation judgment, as AllHipHop previously reported.

In November 2024, New York State won Dash’s one-third Roc-A-Fella stake with a $1 million creditor bid. The state used its creditor claim instead of paying that amount in cash. That was a sale of company equity, not a direct purchase of all rights to Jay-Z’s Reasonable Doubt. It also happened before Dash filed for bankruptcy.

Dash filed for Chapter 7 in Florida in September 2025, listing more than $25 million in debts and $4,350 in personal property. A separate auction that December involved his film company, Poppington, and included rights to “Honor Up.”

Chapter 7 explains why a trustee, rather than Dash, was seeking buyers. The federal courts’ bankruptcy guide describes a process in which the trustee sells assets not protected by exemptions and distributes the proceeds to creditors. Some property can be subject to liens or other creditors’ claims.

Stevenson sought to add Dash’s life-story rights to that effort in August. She argued that his public profile gave them value even though he had not listed them among his bankruptcy assets. In the filing, she wrote:

“[T]he monetization of an individual’s name, image, and likeness has become a well-established and actively regulated commercial market.”

The sale still depended on Everlasting closing the deal within the required period. If the company failed to do so, backup bidder Doug Peters would get the rights for $500,000.

item.title: That Mexican OT Summons A Texas Boogeyman For “CUCUY”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: That Mexican OT set "CUCUY" for October 23, mixing Houston rap with country and blues alongside Kodak Black and Rob49.
item.content:encoded:
Bay City, Texas, rapper That Mexican OT set October 23 for “CUCUY,” a new album named for a boogeyman-like figure in Tejano folklore.

His October 22 announcement detailed a 17-track project with a horror theme built around Houston rap but stretching into country and blues. The guest list includes Kodak Black, Rob49 and 1900Rugrat.

OT had already previewed “Apple Bottom” in the Houston Texans’ “713 Sessions” series, launched October 14. He shared the roof of the team’s stadium with Jeremy Garcia, a classical and flamenco guitarist.

The set also included “Johnny Dang” and “Water,” with the pair perched on a steel truss that supports the retractable roof.

“It was only scary when you looked down,” Garcia told Chron.

The team’s Hustle Town Studio filmed the session as part of a new music series intended to reach people beyond its football audience. The Texans had also sought feedback from NPR’s “Tiny Desk” producers.

That pairing fits the range his team described for the album. “Apple Bottom” pairs country guitar with romantic lyrics, while producer Bankroll Got It brings mariachi-style horns to “Yo Mama,” which features Kodak Black.

The blues thread runs through “I Can’t,” featuring OC Chris, and “The Sickness,” with NASAAN. His team described the latter as pairing raspy vocals with harmonica and a 12-bar structure. On “TSA,” he also switches into Spanish over a faster, four-on-the-floor beat.

OT has long tied his sound to the place he grew up. In a 2023 interview with Chron, he pushed back on listeners who questioned his Southern voice.

“I’ll say I sound southern, but people will say I’m trying to sound like something I’m not. It’s a culture thing.”

He said his Spanish carried a Texas twang and named rappers Big Flake and Lil Bean as others who shared that Texas-Mexican style.

His uncles and cousins had introduced him to Houston’s rap collective Screwed Up Click, with family members making music in a closet studio.

OT also has a November tour with comedian René Vaca on the way. Their pairing follows his earlier work with comedian Ralph Barbosa, who hosted “Lonestar Luchador.”

item.title: Wu-Tang Director Reveals Nas, ODB & Cher Playlist Picks
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Joanna Natasegara explains why Nas, Lauryn Hill, ODB and Cher belong on her playlist for "The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable."
item.content:encoded:
Nas and Lauryn Hill’s 1996 “If I Ruled the World (Imagine That)” captures Cilvaringz’s dream in “The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable,” its director says.

Joanna Natasegara explained her picks in a Tudum interview published October 22. The film follows Cilvaringz, born Tarik Azzougarh, and his one-copy album “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin.”

“This song represents our protagonist Tarik’s aspiration to be a part of the amazing New York music scene led by the Clan,” she said.

Mariah Carey and Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s “Fantasy” remix serves a different purpose. Natasegara said their upbeat team-up plays at one of the film’s high points.

That pairing dates to 1995. The record also drew on a Tom Tom Club sample, bringing another group’s music into Carey’s pop hit, as the Recording Academy noted.

Natasegara also picked “C.R.E.A.M.,” a favorite from Wu-Tang‘s 1993 debut. She credited the Clan’s use of music and film samples for her wide-ranging choices.

The sample in “C.R.E.A.M.” came from the Charmels’ “As Long As I’ve Got You.” Isaac Hayes and David Porter wrote that song, according to Tracklib.

The record did not start in its familiar form. In a 2022 Recording Academy interview, RZA said it went through several versions. One paired him with Ghostface Killah; another ran 12 minutes with Raekwon and Inspectah Deck. That long version was called “Lifestyles Of The Mega Rich.”

When Wu-Tang secured its debut album deal, he wanted the beat on the record. He felt Raekwon and Deck sounded best together, but the song still needed something.

“We needed a hook. And so at the time, the best person to do hooks was Method Man,” RZA said. He described Method Man as the crew’s melodic member, known for sharp hooks.

RZA’s own film work gave him a different set of limits. In that same interview, he said a score has to serve the story. He recalled matching a cue to the moment a character opened her eyes.

Cher’s 1995 cover of Marc Cohn’s “Walking in Memphis” was Natasegara’s surprise pick. Cohn released his version in 1991. She said its place makes sense within the film, but left the connection unexplained.

item.title: Enes Kanter Freedom Rejects Private Suite In WNBA Finals Seat Dispute
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Enes Kanter Freedom said he was denied access to his WNBA Finals seats after refusing the private suite set up for him.
item.content:encoded:
Enes Kanter Freedom wanted the seats he paid for, not a private suite at the WNBA Finals. The former NBA player said security kept him from those seats at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena.

The Associated Press reported that he turned down the suite and left. Freedom gave his own account in a halftime video, saying he had been thrown out.

The Atlanta Dream hosted the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 on Wednesday, October 21. Ludacris was among the music stars in the sold-out crowd, according to the WNBA’s AP recap.

Freedom’s tickets were close to the court, EFE reported. Before the game, he said security would not let him get to those seats and would have to escort him out.

“I purchased tickets, right? Just because I purchased tickets, I would like to sit in my seat. That’s all I want,” Freedom said, according to AP.

His prior WNBA visit ended with an ejection and an arena ban in Chicago. AP reported a heated exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud in late August.

For Atlanta’s arena, the suite was a way to address his safety concerns. In a statement reported by EFE, the venue said Freedom had raised those concerns with federal, state and local authorities. He had also contacted the league, team and arena.

The venue spoke with the league, team owners and security staff before setting up the suite. But the offer came with a condition. EFE reported that someone told Freedom in a halftime video that he could enter only if he agreed to use the suite.

AP said the suite would have extra security. State police had also assigned an officer at his request.

For the Dream, the move to State Farm Arena meant more room for fans. The team’s usual home, Gateway Center Arena, seats 3,500. State Farm Arena can hold more than 17,000. Both Atlanta games sold out.

“Protect home court,” Dream guard Rhyne Howard said of the team’s focus, according to AP. “Giving our fans a show. We fought for this arena so we had to protect it.”

Atlanta won 97-71 to take a 2-1 series lead. Game 4 was set for Saturday, October 24, at the same arena.

item.title: Caleb Williams Gives Drake Ten Spots On His “Madden NFL 27” Playlist
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Caleb Williams picked ten songs featuring Drake for his "Madden NFL 27 Iceman Edition" playlist, mixing solo cuts and guest spots.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams gave Drake ten spots on his “Madden NFL 27 Iceman Edition” playlist, including solo records and guest features.

The Chicago Bears quarterback picked 67 songs for the collection. Apple Music credited Williams as its curator and listed a running time of 3 hours and 43 minutes.

The list opened with Drake’s “Shabang.” Williams also chose “Draft Day,” “Charged Up” and “30 for 30 Freestyle.”

The selections reached beyond Drake’s own releases. His features on Yeat’s “Miss My Dawg,” Future’s “Never Satisfied” and J Hus’ “Who Told You” made the cut, too.

“Chicago Freestyle” with GIVĒON, “6 Man” and “Firm Friends” rounded out the ten Drake-credited selections.

Williams also picked Chance the Rapper’s “No Problem,” with Lil Wayne and 2 Chainz, and Lupe Fiasco’s “Superstar.” Ravyn Lenae’s “Love Me Not” and Leon Thomas’ “Just How You Are” were among the R&B selections.

The Weeknd, Playboi Carti, Lil Durk and Don Toliver also appeared in Apple’s featured-artist list, alongside The White Stripes and Shaboozey.

EA Sports announced the playlist on October 21. Williams is the game’s cover star.

The official Madden NFL account promoted the collection with a short Instagram caption: “Curated by Iceman. Featuring Iceman.” The post directed listeners to Apple Music and described the music as a soundtrack drop.

The nickname also ran through Williams’ Madden cover campaign. The Bears’ behind-the-scenes account said he had earned “Iceman” through his late comeback wins. EA’s creative team built one of its cover concepts around that identity, while the main cover showed his jump throw.

EA Sports creative director Josh Kline said the team began with what made each player different. Williams’ concepts drew on Chicago, his signature moves and Iceman persona. The campaign also used personal touches such as his wired headphones and painted nails.

Williams became the first Bears player on Madden’s main cover. Former Chicago offensive lineman Roberto Garza had appeared on “Madden NFL 09 en Español.” Williams recalled spending hours playing Madden and building his own teams as a child, calling his selection as cover athlete “a dream come true.”

The full collection is available on Apple Music.

item.title: Coco Jones Turns Racist Harassment Into A Masterclass In Dignity & Black Pride
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Coco Jones faced racist harassment during a New York Fashion Week photoshoot and responded with remarkable confidence, Black pride and a kiss that spoke louder than any insult.
item.content:encoded:
WTF is going on in this wrenching place?

Harassing Coco Jones? And yet she won.

Coco Jones managed to embarrass a racist heckler without raising her voice, exchanging insults or even interrupting her New York Fashion Week photoshoot. Now, that is a special kind of composure.

The Grammy Award-winning singer and actress was minding her business in Manhattan when an unidentified woman decided to make her presence known for all the wrong reasons.

Jones was posing for photographs in a stylish Tommy Hilfiger ensemble during September’s Fashion Week festivities. Unfortunately, somebody apparently mistook the public sidewalk for an audition to become America’s most obnoxious pedestrian.

The woman began shouting offensive remarks, including “Ew” and “disgusting,” before making her racial hostility unmistakable.

“You look so freaking Black! Blackie!” the woman shouted.

Imagine thinking somebody’s Blackness is an insult in 2026.

Initially, Jones smiled and offered a polite “Thank you,” apparently before fully registering the hostility directed toward her.

But when the woman’s comments became unmistakably racist, Coco delivered a response that was both simple and magnificent.

“I’m Black and I’m proud.”

That was it.

No screaming match. No elaborate comeback. No security confrontation. Just a declaration of pride delivered with the confidence of somebody who knows exactly who she is.

Jones continued posing, maintained her smile and eventually blew the heckler a kiss before walking away.

The incident appeared in a YouTube vlog Jones published October 20, documenting her New York Fashion Week experience. The footage quickly circulated online, with viewers praising her remarkable restraint.

There is another layer to this unfortunate encounter.

Coco has previously discussed the colorism she experienced while navigating Hollywood, particularly during her earlier years as a Disney performer.

She has spoken openly about learning to reject beauty standards that diminished darker-skinned women. Her journey from Disney actress to Grammy winner makes this encounter especially poignant.

And that is what makes her reaction so compelling.

She did not allow a stranger’s prejudice to dictate her behavior, spoil her moment or diminish her accomplishments.

Now, nobody should be obligated to respond gracefully to racism. Anger would have been perfectly understandable.

Nevertheless, Coco demonstrated that sometimes the most devastating response to ignorance is refusing to entertain it.

The heckler wanted a spectacle.

Coco Jones gave her a fashion show instead.

And somehow, the woman who was doing all that shouting ended up being the one who looked ridiculous.

item.title: Bruno Mars Breaks Kendrick Lamar & SZA’s Chart Record After Drake Detour
item.dc:creator: Adrienne Hunter
item.description: Bruno Mars moved past Kendrick Lamar and SZA as "I Just Might" reached 32 total weeks atop Billboard's R&B/Hip-Hop chart.
item.content:encoded:
Bruno Mars no longer has to share the top spot in the record book with Kendrick Lamar and SZA.

“I Just Might” returned to No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart dated October 24, reaching 32 total weeks there. That moved it past the 31-week mark set by “Luther,” according to Billboard Brasil.

Drake and Don Toliver’s “Solar Eclipse” interrupted Mars’ run for one week before the record-breaking return.

Mars had matched Kendrick and SZA’s record earlier this month. The tie put a solo single from “The Romantic” alongside a duet from Kendrick’s “GNX” that drew on Luther Vandross and Cheryl Lynn’s “If This World Were Mine.”

The single also anchored Mars’ return to solo albums. He released “I Just Might” on January 9 as the first single from “The Romantic.” The nine-song album followed through Atlantic Records on February 27, seven weeks after the single’s release.

It was his fourth solo album and his first since “24K Magic”, a gap of about a decade. In between, he had continued to record with other artists. The run into this project included “Die With A Smile” with Lady Gaga and “APT.” with ROSÉ.

Mars also helped shape videos for the album campaign. He and Daniel Ramos directed the “I Just Might” video, then teamed up again on “Risk It All,” which accompanied the album. The February launch included an iHeartRadio album premiere while Mars went live on TikTok.

The milestone also extended Mars’ history on a chart he had led both alone and with collaborators. His earlier No. 1s included “That’s What I Like,” “Finesse” and “Please Me” with Cardi B, and Silk Sonic’s “Leave The Door Open” with Anderson .Paak.

His Silk Sonic partner was part of the stage plans, too. Before the single arrived, Mars announced The Romantic Tour, his first global headlining tour in nearly a decade and his first full stadium tour. Anderson .Paak was listed for all dates as DJ Pee .Wee, with Leon Thomas, RAYE and Victoria Monét on select shows.

The new record applies to the ranking’s comprehensive history, which began in October 1958.

item.title: DaniLeigh Leaves Revenge Out Of Her Comeback
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: DaniLeigh opened up about forgiveness without an apology as she discussed motherhood, faith and her return to music.
item.content:encoded:
DaniLeigh said she learned to forgive people who hurt her without receiving an apology, bringing a different outlook to her music after years of public relationship drama.

In a new EARMILK interview, the singer explained why she no longer wanted anger to steer her work.

“I’ve learned to forgive people who have hurt me, even when I never received an apology.”

She credited her faith with helping her release resentment and said “With Love, From Dani” was not an attempt to retaliate against anyone. She did not name DaBaby or anyone else in that answer.

The two share a daughter, and their relationship previously played out in public. In November 2021, an argument between them aired on Instagram Live. When DaniLeigh discussed their breakup with Angie Martinez in May 2022, she described a relationship marked by repeated splits and reunions.

At that time, she said they were co-parenting and that DaBaby had not apologized.

In February 2022, DaBaby fought DaniLeigh’s brother, Brandon Bills, at a California bowling alley, TMZ reported. Bills later sued DaBaby, alleging an unprovoked attack. DaBaby had claimed self-defense.

Her music also reflected that period. She released “Dead To Me” alongside the Martinez interview, addressing the relationship through a very different musical message.

DaBaby disputed her account of the split and criticized the timing of “Dead To Me” and the Martinez interview in May 2022.

“Um, first of all, I feel like you waited too late. I told you back in December you should capitalize off the situation,” he said.

TMZ reported in June 2026 that a settlement notice had been filed in Bills’s lawsuit.

In the new conversation, DaniLeigh described motherhood as a reason to weigh the example her songs set. She wanted her daughter to hear strength, self-respect and faith in her work.

In a separate Spanish-language interview with PAPER, DaniLeigh described a limit on what she could write. If someone suggested a breakup song when she was not in that emotional place, she said, she could not do it. The music had to reflect what she was actually living.

She also described making a practical change to “With Love, From Dani” as it neared completion. Feeling that it needed more R&B, she went back through songs she had already made and added others until the project felt cohesive. She wanted the range of sounds to remain recognizably hers.

Working independently gave her a different kind of control, too. In an earlier GQ South Africa interview, she said she could create on her own schedule and owned her masters. She described having considered giving up, but said the chance to make music that helped people feel better gave her a reason to keep going.

item.title: Pharrell Williams Facing Wild Creative Accusations From Chad Hugo Over Neptunes Legacy
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Pharrell Williams faces fierce opposition from former Neptunes pal Chad Hugo.
item.content:encoded:
Pharrell Williams is facing serious allegations from longtime and now former collaborator Chad Hugo.

Hugo maintains that his former friend withheld royalties and songwriting credits from their work as The Neptunes, according to an Oct. 16 federal court filing opposing Williams’ attempt to dismiss the lawsuit.

The disagreement has moved far beyond creative differences.

Hugo claims his longtime collaborator has withheld money and recognition tied to music they produced together.

In an Oct. 16 federal court filing, Hugo’s attorneys urged a judge to reject Pharrell’s attempt to dismiss the lawsuit. Their argument portrays the dispute as a fight over more than unpaid royalties. They contend that Pharrell seeks to diminish Hugo’s historical contributions to the production team.

Hugo’s lawyers characterized the situation as an “effort to rewrite history and turn The Neptunes’ success into the work of only one person,” according to a report from The Jasmine Brand.

“Defendants ask the Court to write Chad Hugo out of The Neptunes on the pleadings, before a single document has been produced,” the filing states. “But The Neptunes were two people.”

For decades, Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo operated as The Neptunes, helping define the sound of contemporary Hip-Hop and R&B. Their partnership established them as one of the music industry’s most recognizable production teams, with a creative reputation built on their collective work.

According to Hugo’s allegations, the two producers reached an agreement in 2019 to share production revenue and publishing rights equally. Hugo maintains that Williams subsequently retained earnings and recognition associated with compositions they created together.

The complaint reportedly addresses nearly 50 recording sessions conducted between 2019 and 2021.

Among the disputed recordings is EarthGang’s “U Gotta,” which Hugo claims he helped create without receiving appropriate acknowledgment.

Pharrell and company have challenged the lawsuit, arguing that Hugo has failed to identify the disputed musical compositions with sufficient specificity.

Their request for dismissal focuses on whether the complaint meets the legal requirements necessary for the case to proceed.

Hugo’s attorneys reject that position and maintain that the dispute deserves further examination through the litigation process.

Hugo initially filed his lawsuit in January, seeking recognition of his copyright ownership and a financial accounting of revenue generated from the contested works.

His legal team has also requested permission to amend the complaint within 21 days if the court determines that additional information is necessary.

The allegations remain contested, and the court has not established that Williams improperly withheld royalties or denied Hugo ownership rights.
